C-SPEC-LINT-RULES-SPLIT-R1.Summary: Split the 1766-line src/lib/spec-lint.ts rule monolith into zone modules under src/lib/spec-lint/ while keeping src/lib/spec-lint.ts itself as the re-export-only public barrel, so every ../lib/spec-lint.js import keeps resolving under moduleResolution NodeNext.
C-SPEC-LINT-RULES-SPLIT-R1.Problem: spec-lint.ts is a pure, well-scoped linter but internally monolithic: only 6 exports are public while roughly 1500 lines of private rule functions for all artifact kinds, cross-file checks, delegated extraction, and parsing sit in one file. The superseded C-SPEC-LINT-RULES-SPLIT plan intended to replace the file with a directory barrel at src/lib/spec-lint/index.ts, but under TypeScript moduleResolution NodeNext the specifier ../lib/spec-lint.js never resolves to a directory index, so deleting the file would break every consumer. This replacement keeps the reviewed intent with the NodeNext-valid barrel placement.

Goals.Goal: src/lib/spec-lint/ with parser.ts, spec-rules.ts, plan-rules.ts, cross-file-rules.ts, and delegated-extraction.ts zone modules; src/lib/spec-lint.ts remains at its path as a re-export-only barrel preserving the complete current public API.
Behavior-preserving: identical findings, severities, rule ids, line numbers, cache keys, and extraction results for the same inputs; LINT_VERSION stays 2.
M-SPEC-LINT remains the owning graph module with Paths updated to the barrel plus zone files and spec-lint-cache.ts untouched.

Constraints.Constraint: Pure structural move: no rule semantics, finding text, severity mapping, LINT_VERSION bump, or public API change.
src/lib/spec-lint.ts is a re-export barrel only: no rule implementation and no htmlparser2 import; its imports are limited to ./spec-lint/*.js zone modules.

Zone boundaries: parser.ts (xmlMode event-stream parse, positioned element tree, artifact-kind detection, archive-path check), spec-rules.ts (spec and design-context template/identity rules), plan-rules.ts (plan template, task/wave/checkpoint identity and reference rules, execution-section and review-checkpoint rules), cross-file-rules.ts (plan-subset-of-spec and cross-artifact checks), delegated-extraction.ts (extractDelegatedPlanDefinition and typed helpers); lintSpecArtifacts orchestration lives in a lint.ts zone module re-exported by the barrel.
src/lib/spec-lint.test.ts and src/lib/spec-lint-cache.test.ts stay at their current paths and content; all consumers keep importing ../lib/spec-lint.js.
Shared private helpers live in exactly one zone module; no duplication.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No new lint rules, no rule relaxations or tightenings, no cache format change, no tsconfig change.
No changes to spec-lint-cache.ts, the spec-guard plugin, commands/lint.ts, or workflow-contract re-exports.
No new graph modules; M-SPEC-LINT keeps owning the linter.
No test additions or renames; the existing suites passing unmodified are the behavior-preservation evidence.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: src/lib/spec-lint.ts exists as a re-export-only barrel over the zone modules re-exporting the complete previous public API; ../lib/spec-lint.js and ./spec-lint.js keep resolving and typechecking for every consumer, including spec-lint-cache.ts and both test files.
AC-02: Rule functions are distributed into the zone modules with truthful file-local contracts, maps, and change summaries linking M-SPEC-LINT; shared helpers exist once.
AC-03: bun test on src/lib/spec-lint.test.ts, src/lib/spec-lint-cache.test.ts, and src/plugins/spec-guard/index.test.ts passes unmodified; bun run check, build, and pack:check pass.
AC-04: M-SPEC-LINT Paths list src/lib/spec-lint.ts plus the zone files and the unchanged spec-lint-cache.ts, Purpose/Depends/Verification stay truthful, and grace lint and grace status pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun run build && bun run pack:check
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Target assertions verify the zone files and barrel re-exports exist with no htmlparser2 in the barrel; the unmodified linter, cache, and spec-guard suites through the barrel are the behavior-preservation evidence.

Assumptions.Assumption: A rule function may move to an adjacent zone during execution when its inputs reveal a clearer owner, recorded in the change summary, without adding or removing zones.

Approval provenance: the user approved the reviewed five-item refactoring list and explicitly instructed autonomous grace-plan/grace-execute execution; this replacement corrects only the barrel placement discovered under NodeNext and inherits that authorization.
